artifact_types: default destructive-pattern table with near-miss pass cases
local guard installation receipt or refusal
forbidden_actions: request, reveal, print, persist, hash, or transmit credential or secret values
perform source, local-system, browser, provider, publication, or remote mutations outside the exact atomic scope and fresh authorization
invent commands, exits, duration, artifacts, captures, provider receipts, benchmark results, approval, or completion evidence
combine independent evidence or findings with remediation, risk acceptance, publication, deployment, or release
claim evaluation, approval, release, or completion evidence that has not been produced
hard_gates: Guard authoring may create tested repository artifacts but cannot modify Git config, hook paths, aliases, shell startup, or enable interception without separate local-system authorization.
Independent review, QA, audit, acquisition, analysis, and triage never imply remediation; setup or authentication never implies downstream action authority.
Never silently enable a guard or modify a committed, shared, custom, or ambiguous hooks directory; explicit consent, backup, verification, and uninstall are mandatory.
inputs: A command hook environment, dangerous-command policy, and local configuration.
Repository Git-dir evidence, hooks-path classification, guard artifact, user consent, and local-system write authorization.
outputs: default destructive-pattern table with near-miss pass cases
local guard installation receipt or refusal
permission_identity_is_default: most common of mode_permissions; the effective identity for a run is mode_permissions[selected_mode]
responsibility: Consolidated capability covering 2 related modes: Author and validate a repository-scoped guard policy that intercepts declared destructive Git command patterns before execution without installing it silently.; Install or configure one approved repository-local Git guard after classifying the hooks path, with consent, verification, backup, and uninstall instructions.
